title: Can I BEAT Cornered Kings?
summary: chess.com variant Cornered (by BlueYoshi21) vs humans (~1500-1800): 10x8 board whose four left files are stone except two corridors; each royal king (fleur-de-lis) starts in a corridor and wins by reaching the shaded hill square at its end (d6 / d3) or by checkmate. Each side also has a non-royal king, Dragon Knights (non-jumping knight), Sergeants (fW+fF), Soldiers (fW), a Bishop and a Knight; promotion to General or Rook on the rank of your royal king. Red moves first.
rules: Royal king must reach its highlighted square (hill) to win; checkmate also wins (0:01; variants.world KotH f6,f9 + Play for Mate).
Second king of each side is a normal non-royal piece (0:06).
Dragon Knight = knight that cannot jump; Sergeant = move/capture forward or diagonally forward; Soldier = move/capture straight ahead (0:10-0:12).
Promotion to General (K+N) or Rook on the rank level with your royal king (variant page: =MR, 9th rank in FEN4 = rank 6 for Red).
Stalemate loses; Red moves first (0:26); 3 minutes, no increment (3:26).
win_condition: Royal king onto its hill square, or checkmate the enemy royal king.
player_side: red (moves first; both stills); yellow in game 1

board.shape_notes: files a-d stone except ranks 6 and 3 (royal corridors: royal K a6/a3, non-royal enemy K c6/c3, hill d6/d3); play area e-j
board.theme_notes: grey chess.com variants board, cobblestone walls, shaded hill squares
